title: Go: Background Task Queue
description: Build a background task queue in Go with priority scheduling, worker pools, retries with backoff, and scheduled jobs.

steps.title: Job struct with priority
steps.description: Define a `Job` struct with `ID string`, `Priority int`, `Payload func() error`, `CreatedAt time.Time`. Create a few jobs with different priorities and print them sorted by priority to verify ordering.
hints: Use `type Job struct { ID string; Priority int; Payload func() error; CreatedAt time.Time }`
Implement `String()` method on Job for pretty printing with fmt.Stringer interface

verification.successMessage: Job struct with priority and payload function is properly defined!
verification.failureMessage: Print each job's ID and priority using fmt.Printf.

steps.title: Priority queue with container/heap
steps.description: Implement a `PriorityQueue` that implements `heap.Interface` (Len, Less, Swap, Push, Pop). Use `container/heap` to manage jobs by priority (higher value = higher priority). Push 5 jobs with varied priorities, pop them one by one, and print the order to verify highest priority comes first.
hints: Define `type PriorityQueue []*Job` and implement the 5 heap.Interface methods
`Less` should return `pq[i].Priority > pq[j].Priority` for max-heap behavior
Use `heap.Push(&pq, job)` and `heap.Pop(&pq)` — not direct slice append/pop

verification.successMessage: Priority queue with container/heap correctly returns highest priority jobs first!
verification.failureMessage: Print jobs in the order they are popped — highest priority should come first.

steps.title: Worker pool with goroutines
steps.description: Create a `WorkerPool` with a configurable number of workers. Each worker runs in a goroutine, pulls jobs from a shared channel, executes them, and reports completion. Use a `sync.WaitGroup` to wait for all workers to finish. Submit 10 jobs to a pool of 3 workers and print execution results.
hints: Create worker goroutines in a loop: `for i := 0; i < n; i++ { go w.worker(i) }`
Each worker reads from `jobs <-chan *Job` and calls `job.Payload()`
Print which worker executed each job: `fmt.Printf("Worker %d processed %s\n", id, job.ID)`

verification.successMessage: Worker pool with goroutines processes jobs concurrently across multiple workers!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Worker X processed job Y' for each completed job.

steps.title: Retry with exponential backoff
steps.description: Implement retry logic for failed jobs. Wrap the job payload with a `Retry` decorator that retries up to `maxRetries` times with exponential backoff (100ms, 200ms, 400ms, ...). Print "Attempt X failed" on failure and "Job succeeded after X attempts" on success. Print "Job failed permanently" if all retries are exhausted.
hints: Create a `Retry(payload func() error, maxRetries int) func() error` wrapper
Print each attempt: `fmt.Printf("Attempt %d failed: %v\n", attempt+1, err)`

verification.successMessage: Retry with exponential backoff correctly retries failed jobs and reports results!
verification.failureMessage: Print each retry attempt and the final success or permanent failure message.

steps.title: Scheduled jobs with timer
steps.description: Implement a `Scheduler` that runs jobs at specified intervals. Add `Schedule(job *Job, interval time.Duration)` that runs the job periodically using `time.NewTicker`. Support `Cancel(id)` to stop a scheduled job. Schedule two jobs with different intervals, let them run for a few ticks, then cancel one. Print execution timestamps.
hints: Store `map[string]*time.Ticker` for active scheduled jobs on the scheduler
Launch a goroutine for each scheduled job that reads from the ticker channel
Print with timestamps: `fmt.Printf("[%s] Running %s\n", time.Now().Format("15:04:05"), job.ID)`

verification.successMessage: Scheduler correctly runs periodic jobs and stops them on cancellation!
verification.failureMessage: Print periodic execution timestamps and confirm cancellation with 'Cancelled: <job>'.
